title: Quarterly roadmap: Elasticity Runways & Surge Signal Matrix for Dedicated Pools
creator: Marina Kline
description:
Objective: Define a pragmatic, roll-forward quarterly roadmap to increase Dedicated pool elasticity while preserving latency SLOs and predictable unit economics. We will produce: (1) an operational "elasticity runway" playbook that codifies prewarm windows, reservation hedges, and burst-to-fallback policies; (2) a Surge Signal Matrix that maps real telemetry signals -> automated actions (e.g., prewarm, scale, degrade, fallback); and (3) dashboards + canary criteria to validate each policy in production.

Scope: Dedicated GPU pools (all instance families) for hosted and dedicated customers. Work focuses on control-plane orchestration (policy DSL), telemetry thresholds, cost guardrails, and runbooks for oncall. Not in scope: new GPU types, hardware procurement, or dedicated-private installation packaging.

Success criteria (end of quarter):
- Documented Elasticity Runway playbook with 3 concrete reservation/hedge recipes for low/medium/high burst scenarios.
- Surge Signal Matrix adopted by autoscaler service and wired to existing fallback routes.
- Dashboards showing SLO health (P50/P95/P99 tail-latency), cold-start rate, and token cost delta; baseline compared to start-of-quarter.
- One canary rollout that validates a hedge policy with <2% customer error delta and <=5% cost uplift during trial.

Key trade-offs discussed:
- Aggressive prewarm reduces tail latency but increases short-term cost; we will codify tiered hedges (conservative/neutral/aggressive) per customer SLA.
- Centralized vs per-pool policies: centralized simplifies governance but may under-optimize for tenants with skewed load patterns. Plan: default centralized policies with pool-level overrides for high-commit customers.

Milestones & deliverables:
- Week 1 (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07): Signal inventory + telemetry queries (owner: ENG infra).
- Week 2: Draft Surge Signal Matrix + initial playbook draft (owner: PM).
- Week 3: Policy DSL sketch and autoscaler integration plan (owner: ENG runtime).
- Week 4: Dashboard PR + canary plan; stakeholder review (owner: Observability).
- Week 5: Implement canary, run trial, capture metrics.

Stakeholders: SRE oncall, Runtime (batching & KV cache), Observability, Sales engineering (for high-commit customers), Solutions.

notes: Do not run aggressive hedges for pools with active regulatory constraints (private installs) until a security review is completed. PM will coordinate with Security if any dedicated-private customers are selected for trials.
